content:
raj: Quick datapoint — during the blue-green flip for model-variant B we saw a ~12% error spike that traced back to KV prefixes being evicted on the old pool and then repeatedly re-prefetched on the new pool. Causes a traffic storm on cold prefixes.
sophia: Interesting. Was that tenant-level eviction credit transfer happening?
raj: Yes. Our soft-evict credits are per-shard and we were doing an instant migration. Credits didn't follow the tenant, so the new pool treated most prefixes as cold.
matt: Oof. So migration = effective cache reset for those prefixes. Any TL;DR on why credits can't be moved today?
raj: Two reasons: (1) credits are stored in local slab metadata tied to instance id, and (2) we don't have a lease handoff RPC for credit buckets. Moving them would require cross-instance coordination + safety for concurrent access.
elaine: Could we shadow-prefetch immediate after migration for the active tenant only? That reduces user-visible errors but still wastes tokens.
jen: What about transferring a lightweight summary instead of full credits? e.g., transfer a compact histogram of recent access freq and a hot-key set.
sophia: I like the summary idea. The invariant we need: after migration, we must avoid both (A) cold re-fetch storm and (B) double-counting credits that allow two pools to think they own the same hot entries.
raj: Proposed sketch: 
```
migration-step-1: freeze writes to shard metadata (short lock)
migration-step-2: serialize compact access summary: top-N hot prefixes + last-access-sentinel
migration-step-3: install summary on target pool and attach a transient lease token
migration-step-4: allow target to ramp inference with summary-driven prefetch, dial down after window
```
This avoids moving full credit slabs and keeps handoff cheap.
matt: How do we ensure correctness if requests still land on source pool during the handoff window? Race with writes to KV residency.
raj: The short lock in step-1 only needs to protect the summary snapshot; we don't need to quiesce the whole shard. For writes we can use per-prefix sequence numbers in the summary: target will compare and fetch deltas for any prefix whose seq > snapshot_seq.
elaine: That sounds like a mini-lease + delta-fetch. But seq numbers mean we must guarantee monotonicity across the migration. Do we have that in the current prefix metadata?
sophia: We have per-prefix monotonic counters for apply indices in the sequencer, but they don't live in the slab. We can export sequencer index + rsync a small delta. Slight overhead but doable.
jen: Metrics to watch: prefetch-rps on target in first 30s, duplicate-fetch-rate (same prefix fetched by both pools), and prefetched-wasted-tokens. If duplicate-fetch-rate > 0.5% we fail the rollout.
raj: Also add read-after-write correctness check: any write that raced must be visible on first read on the target. That means delta-fetch must be synchronous for those prefixes (block first request with short timeout).
matt: Synchronous blocking for a tiny set of prefixes is okay if we cap to top-N. What's a safe N? 100-1000 depending on tenant size.
sophia: Add an adaptive N: pick enough hot prefixes to cover 95th percentile of recent token volume. We can compute that from the histogram.
elaine: Operational concerns: what if target fails mid-window? We should have a rollback path where source resumes ownership and drains the transient lease after TTL.
jen: Prefetch-bot: added automated prefetch dashboard + alert:prefetch-storm for new migrations. Will produce synthetic load test showing best-case/worst-case numbers. :robot_face:
raj: Implementation tasks: 1) export compact summary proto, 2) lease token + transient attach/detach API, 3) delta fetch RPC, 4) migration orchestration in deploy-runner.
matt: Can we reuse existing lease infra? I don't want a second control plane.
raj: We can reuse sequencer leases for exclusivity check, but need a tiny RPC glue to transfer summary + token.
sophia: Security: ensure summaries don't leak tenant data. The summary is just prefix ids and counts (no payload), but mark it encrypted in transit.
elaine: Perf micro-optimization: instead of prefetching full kv entries, allow lightweight warm reads that prime cache meta then lazy fetch value on demand. Cuts immediate token cost.
jen: +1 to lazy value fetch. We'll simulate both in the prefetch-bot tests.
raj: Next steps: I'll open an RFC with the summary proto + sequence semantics. Volunteers for review: @matt @sophia @elaine. Aim to get prototype in next sprint.
sophia: I'll review the proto. Also let's list the failure modes in the RFC (partial migration, double-prefetch loops, seq desync).
matt: I'll pair on the orchestration side. Thanks. :thumbsup:
